abstraction_design.rationale: Real abstractions exist and hold up (card, move table, data services, helpers), but the app's central repeated concept — a list of Pokémon cards derived from pokemon refs — is copy-pasted three times with per-page sprite wiring, so similar-but-different features start from a copy.

findings.issue: The 'build a list of Pokémon cards from pokemon refs' derivation (species map, drop alternate forms, dedupe, sort, humanize) is copy-pasted across move-page, ability-page and type-page loaders, so any change to card lists (sorting, types on cards, sprite fix) must be made three times.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single helper (e.g. PokedexData.cardsForPokemonRefs(refs, extras?) or a shared CardListModel builder in core/) that returns {id, name, displayName, spriteUrl} once, and have all three pages call it.

findings.issue: Sprite URL policy is caller-side: three pages each define their own `spriteUrl = (id) => this.api.spriteUrl(id)` lambda, while home-page uses `front_default ?? pattern` and pokemon-page uses a three-way artwork fallback — a sprite bug fix has no single home.
findings.suggestion: Move the policy into the shared layer: either let PokemonCard derive its sprite from the species id (or a passed default-Pokémon record), or return spriteUrl from the shared card-list builder so pages stop deciding.

findings.issue: HomePage keeps a `view` signal that mirrors the resource's value via an effect (lines 196-198), creating two representations of the same data that must be kept in sync when editing the page.
findings.suggestion: Drop the shadow signal and use the resource directly (resource keeps the previous value during reload); if stale-while-reload behavior is needed, encapsulate it in one place (e.g. a computed that caches the last resolved value) rather than an effect assignment.

findings.issue: `isAlternateForm` is defined but never used — the `> 10000` rule is inlined three times in page loaders (move-page.ts:112, ability-page.ts:76, type-page.ts:112) and inverted once in pokedex-data.ts:163 (`id <= 10_000`).
findings.suggestion: Use the helper everywhere (it also makes the rule greppable if the cutoff ever changes).

findings.issue: Three implementations of 'missing value → em dash': helpers.ts:65 `displayValue` (never called), move-page.ts:96 `display`, move-table.ts:118 `display`.
findings.suggestion: Delete the two local copies and export/use `displayValue` from helpers.

findings.issue: The 'set document title from the loaded resource' effect is duplicated in four pages (type, ability, move, pokemon) plus constructor titles elsewhere — a behaviour change to titles means four edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a tiny `setPageTitle(label)` helper or use the router's TitleStrategy so the `<h1> – Pokédex` rule lives in one place.

findings.issue: `PokeApi.media()` is dead code — no caller anywhere in src/.
findings.suggestion: Remove it, or use it as the single place that resolves sprite/artwork URLs (which would also address the sprite-policy spread).

findings.issue: Hash-scrolling to #moves is done with an effect + setTimeout + getElementById, which is fragile to template refactors (the `id='moves'` string is duplicated in the template at line 162 and here).
findings.suggestion: Use Angular's built-in anchor scrolling (withViewTransition/ViewportScroller or a router scroll config), or at least reference the section via a template ref variable.

findings.issue: Each column header wires two click handlers (th + nested button with stopPropagation) — duplicated event plumbing per column that a future column addition must copy exactly.
findings.suggestion: Keep a single handler on the th (with a button inside for semantics) or generate the header cells from a column-descriptor array.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is declared as a dependency but never imported anywhere in src/, and the app ships a `ng test` script with zero unit tests, so loader/sorting changes have no fast safety net.
findings.suggestion: Drop the unused dependency and add a few Vitest specs for the card-list derivation and MoveTable sorting once they're centralized.

summary: This is a clean, current-idiom Angular 22 codebase: standalone signal components, layered data services, input-based shared UI, and total separation of the Node static server. Its weakness is systematic copy-paste of the app's central concept — building a list of Pokémon cards — across three page loaders, with the sprite policy and alternate-form rule duplicated alongside it, so cross-cutting changes land N times. Removal and data-source changes are easy; behaviour fixes and new similar features are where the friction is.
